units: <cite ref="Berakhot 7b:10">Ber. 7ᵇ</cite> <he>מיום שברא … שקְרָאוֹ … וּקְרָאוֹ אדון</he> from the day that the Lord created the world there was no man that called the Holy One, blessed be He, lord, until Abraham came and called him lord (<cite ref="Genesis 15:2">Gen. XV, 2</cite> <cite ref="A00435"><he>אדני</he></cite>).
Gen. R. s. 56 אברהם קראו יראה Abraham called it (the Temple site) yeraëh (Gen. XXII, 14), שם ק׳ אותו שלם Shem called it Salem (ib. XIV, 18), הריני קוֹרֵא אותו ירושלם I will call it Jerusalem.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 70b:15">Snh. 70ᵇ</cite> <he>אין … לִקְרוֹא אבא וכ׳</he> no sooner does a child know to call ‘father’ and ‘mother’, than it tastes grain food.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 15:13">Num. R. s. 15</cite>, beg. <he>ק׳ אותו אוהב</he> he invited that friend.

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 15:13">Ib.</cite> <he>והיה קורא אומניות</he>, v. <cite ref="A00708"><he>אוּמָנוּת</he></cite>; a. v. fr.—Part. pass. <cite ref="S01923"><he>קָרוּא</he></cite>, <cite ref="S01935"><he>קָרוּי</he></cite>; f. <he>קְרוּאָה</he>, <cite ref="S01940"><he>קְרוּיָה</he></cite>; Pl. <he>קְרוּאִים</he>, <he>קְרוּאִין</he>, <he>קְרוּיִים</he>, <he>קְרוּיִם</he>, <he>קְרוּיִין</he>, <he>קְרוּיִן</he>; <cite ref="S01941"><he>קְרוּאוֹת</he></cite>, <cite ref="S01941"><he>קְרוּיוֹת</he></cite>.

B. Mets. 114ᵇ, a. e. (ref. to Ez. XXXIV, 31) אתם ק׳ אדם וכ׳ you are called men, but idolaters &c. Sifra Aḥăré, end כל העריות ק׳ טומאה all illicit connections are called uncleanness; a. fr.—Esp. קְרוּאִים, קְרוּיִין those called up to read from the Torah (v. infra).

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 70:5">Gen. R. s. 70</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 29:2">Gen. XXIX, 2</cite>) <he>אלו שלשה ק׳</he> this is typical of the three persons called up to read from the Torah (priest, Levite, and Israelite).
Y. Meg. III, 74ᵇ ולא שבעה ק׳ אינון are not seven persons called up (on the Sabbath)?; a. fr.—V. קְרוּיוֹת.—2) to read, recite (esp. from the Scriptures).

<cite ref="Mishnah Yoma 1:6">Yoma I, 6</cite> <he>אם רגיל לִקְרוֹת … קוֹרִין לפניו</he> if he (the high priest) is accustomed to read (the Scriptures), he reads himself, if not, they read to him; <he>ובמה קורין לפניו</he> and from what books do they read to him? <cite ref="Mishnah Yoma 1:6">Ib.</cite> <he>פעמים הרבה קָרִיתִי וכ׳</he> many a time I read to him from Daniel.
<cite ref="Mishnah Megillah 2:1">Meg. II, 1</cite> <he>הקורא את המגילה וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="M02249"><he>מִפְרֵעַ</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Megillah 2:2">Ib. 2</cite> <he>קְרָאָהּ סירוגין</he>, v. <cite ref="O00836"><he>סֵירוּג</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Megillah 2:3">Ib. 3</cite> <he>קורא כמקומו</he> he must read in accordance with the usage of the place he came from.
<cite ref="Mishnah Megillah 2:4">Ib. 4</cite> <he>הכל כשרין לִקְרוֹת וכ׳</he> all persons are qualified to recite the Book of Esther (before the congregation).

Y. Meg. IV, 74ᵈ bot. וקְרָיָיהּ and read from it; a. fr.—Esp. to read from the Torah at public services. Ib. III, 4 קורין בפרשת שקלים they (those who are called up, v. supra) read the section of Sheḳalim (Ex. XXX, 11-16). Ib. 6 אחד קורא את כולן one person must read the entire chapter (of the curses). Ib. IV, 1 בשני … קורין שלשה on Mondays … three persons read. Ib. 4 הקורא בתורה לא יפחות וכ׳ he who is designated to read from the Torah must read no less than three verses; לא יִקְרָא למתורגמן וכ׳ he must read to the interpreter one verse at a time, but from the Prophets, three verses.

Bicc. I, 1 יש מביאין … וקורין וכ׳ there are those who are bound to bring the first-fruits and to read (Deut. XXVI, 5-10), and those who must bring but not read &c. Ib. 4; a. v. fr.—Esp. (את שמע) ק׳ to recite the Sh’mʿa in the morning and in the evening prayer.
<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 1:1">Ber. I, 1</cite> <he>לא קָרִינוּ וכ׳</he> we omitted to read the Sh’mʿa.
<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 2:3">Ib. II, 3</cite> <he>ק׳ וטעה</he> if one read the Sh’mʿa and made a mistake.

Ib. 4 האומנין קוֹרְאִין וכ׳ (Bab. ed. 16ᵃ קורין) workingmen read the Sh’mʿa on top of a tree, or on the scaffolding; a. v. fr.—אל תִּקְרֵי … אלא (or תִּיקְרִי Chald. form; abbrev. א״ת) read not … but—, i.e. change the traditional (Massoretic) reading (for homiletical purposes). Ib. 64ᵃ (ref. to Is. LIV, 13 א״ת בָּנַיִךְ אלא בּוֹנַיִךְ read not banayikh (thy children) but bonayikh (thy builders, the scholars).
M. Kat. 9ᵇ (ref. to Ps. XLIX, 12) א״ת קִרְבָּם אלא קִבְרָם read not ḳirbam (their innermost) but ḳibram (their grave); a. fr.

senses.gloss: same, to call, invite. Part. pass. מְקוֹרָא, pl. מְקוֹרָאִים, מְקוֹרָאִין.
units: <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 13:14">Num. R. s. 13</cite> <he>יש חתן … למק׳ וכ׳</he> does a bridegroom give a banquet for the invited guests and not sit with them?; a. e.
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 1:13">Lev. R. s. 1</cite>, beg. <he>נִקְרְאוּ הנביאים וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="B00753"><he>בַּיִת</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 1:33">Ex. R. s. 1</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Exodus 2:13">Ex. II, 13</cite>) <he>מכאן … נ׳ רשע</he> from here we learn that when a man lifts up his hand to strike his neighbor, even if he does not strike, he is called a wicked man; <cite ref="Sanhedrin 58b">Snh. 58ᵇ</cite>.
Ab. Zar. 19ᵃ (ref. to Ps. I, 2) בתחלה נִקְרֵאת … נקראת וכ׳ first it (the Law) is called the Lord’s, and then his (the student’s); a. fr.— to be read, recited.

<cite ref="Mishnah Megillah 1:1">Meg. I, 1</cite> <he>מגלה נקראת וכ׳</he> the Book of Esther may be read at public service on the eleventh &c. Ib. IV, 10 <he>מעשה ראובן נ׳ ולא וכ׳</he> the story of Reuben (<cite ref="Genesis 35:22">Gen. XXXV, 22</cite>) is read at public service but not translated.

<cite ref="Genesis 35:22">Ib.</cite> <he>לא נִקְרָאִין וכ׳</he> (Y. ed. <cite ref="N00689"><he>נִיקְרִין</he></cite>) must be neither read nor interpreted. Tosef. ib. IV (III), 31 <he>יש נקראין ומתרגמין וכ׳</he> certain verses are read but not interpreted &c.; <cite ref="Megillah 25a:18">Meg. 25ᵃ</cite> <he>נִקְרִין</he>; a. v. fr.

senses.gloss: to cause to call, to lead in reading.
units: Sot. 10ᵃ sq. (ref. to Gen. XXI, 33) א״ת וַיִּקְרָא אלא וַיַּקְרִיא read not vayiḳra (and he called) but vayaḳri (and he made call), מלמד שה׳ וכ׳ intimating that Abraham caused the name of the Lord to be called by the mouth of every passer-by. Y. ib. V, 20ᶜ top קטן שהוא מַקְרֵא וכ׳ a child that reads the Hallel at school, and they (the class) respond by repeating each sentence (v. עָנָה I); גדול שהוא מקרא וכ׳ an adult that leads in reciting …, when the congregation responds with the first sentence (as refrain).
<cite ref="Mishnah Sukkah 3:10">Succ. III, 10</cite> <he>מי שהיה … מַקְרִין אותו וכ׳</he> if a slave, a woman, or a child reads to him, he responds with Hallelujah.
Gitt. III, 1 שמע קול סופרים מקרין וכ׳ heard the teaching scribes as they made the practicing children read, ‘such and such … divorces &c.’—Esp. to teach the Scriptures (מִקְרָא).

<cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 1:44">Lam. R. to I, 6</cite> <he>הַקְרינִי דף אחד … השניני וכ׳</he> teach me a page of the Scriptures, teach me a chapter of the Mishnah; a. fr.—[<cite ref="Eruvin 104b:10">Erub. 104ᵇ</cite> <he>שהקרו</he>, v. <cite ref="S02193"><he>קָרַר</he> I</cite>.]
